page: Microsoft Azure F2as_v6 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Fasv6 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The F2as_v6 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core testing. However, multi-core and memory-bound workloads show limitations. Multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average and weak categories respectively, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3781.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth at 38.2 GB/sec and small block cached bandwidth at 294.84 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 25%.

Given its hardware profile, the F2as_v6 is suited for workloads that prioritize single-threaded CPU performance over high memory throughput or multi-threaded scaling. Appropriate workloads include light single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM inference, where it achieves average speeds of 573.44 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 135M model. It is less suited for memory-intensive database operations, software compilation, or high-throughput web serving due to weak performance in those benchmark categories. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable single-core execution, but the low memory bandwidth and lack of local storage represent clear resource tradeoffs.
